# Early co-occurrence network openness is associated with cross-disciplinary concept breadth: evidence from 12,499 scientific concepts

## Overview

This paper asks which early structural signals in a concept's topic co-occurrence network anticipate later cross-field breadth. Using 12,499 concepts from the OpenAlex bulk snapshot, we screen 53 early network indicators from six families against a popularity baseline on held-out field groups and a confirmatory onset cohort.

## Key findings

- Seven indicators survive held-out validation; from the ego-network family we build the six-component OPEN index (pooled partial Spearman +0.069 with rarefied breadth).
- Concepts spread next to fields related to those currently retaining them (d0 = 0.322), but the pre-registered verdict is PARTIAL.
- Early ideational consistency predicts volume but narrower cross-field reach.
- Early contact diversity accounts for 77.9% of the breadth gap between integrating and localised concepts.
- On held-out bodies (n=1,833), ElasticNet combining all 53 indicators reaches Spearman 0.765.

## Files

- `paper.tex` — LaTeX source
- `paper.pdf` — compiled PDF
- `references.bib` — bibliography
- `index.html` — companion website
- `figures/` — all figures (fig_overview_v0.jpg, fig_evidence_synthesis_v0.pdf, fig_entry_v0.pdf, fig_case_study_v0.pdf)

## Code

Analysis code: https://github.com/ai-inventor-papers/ai-invention-8795ea-concepts-spread-once-adopters-make-them/tree/fork/run_MjdbXJqg-rPl
